title: Response to proposed United States tariffs
subtitle: Council gave feedback on the Kitchener 2051 Official Plan's Big Ideas and met in closed session.
overview: Council's special meeting on February 10, 2025 centred on the proposed United States tariffs on Canadian goods. The Mayor brought forward a notice of motion on how the tariffs could affect Kitchener's economy. It would direct staff to look at ways to limit the impact, including a Buy Canadian preference in City purchasing where the law allows. The minutes record no vote on the motion at this meeting.

The motion also proposes a shared action plan with local businesses and neighbouring municipalities. It would have the City press the Province for clear guidance on procurement, support national and provincial municipal advocacy on trade, and encourage residents to buy Canadian and local. Staff would report back if tariffs take effect. This matters to residents because it affects local jobs and how the City spends public money.

Council also held a strategic session on the new Official Plan, Kitchener 2051. Staff asked members for input on strategies for three Big Ideas: Neighbourhoods, Economy and Environments. No motion was recorded. Staff expect to bring a draft plan forward in early fall 2025, after more community engagement. Council then agreed to meet in closed session on six matters.

decisions.item: Response to proposed United States tariffs
decisions.detail: The Mayor brought forward a notice of motion directing staff to find ways to reduce tariff impacts, including a legally permitted Buy Canadian procurement preference, and to report back if tariffs take effect; the minutes record no vote.
